newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swede designs urine-soaked fish anorak for cold.
newsitem.headline: Swede designs urine-soaked fish anorak for cold.

text.p: As Swedes brace themselves for the start of a long, cold winter, artist Ann-Kristin Antman has come up with a Stone Age design especially for the cold climate -- an anorak made of urine-soaked salmon skin.
Antman, from Vuollerim in far north Sweden, made the coat from the skins of 20 salmon weighing 15 kilos (33 pounds) each, Swedish tabloid Aftonbladet reported on Monday.
She then soaked the coat in five litres (11 pints) of urine collected from members of her family.

"It is a method used during the Stone Age in Sweden," Antman said. "Eskimos hardened fish skin in urine and made raincoats and even shoes from it. It protects well from the rain and rough weather and it really hard-wearing.
"The smell disappears when you rinse the skins in water," Antman reassured all potential fashion victims.

But although the anorak is entirely made from natural products, the price is not so basic. At 75,000 crowns ($11,345) each, fish anoraks are not likely to be reeled in at high street stores this winter.
